I've been doing this rotation for as long as I can remember. My mother did it before me. I know this land — what it needs, when it's thirsty, what the neighbors are planting. My two children work in the city now, so it's mostly me and my husband doing the field work, with hired tractor service for the heavy jobs.

**Wheat (winter, starting October):**
I'll plant wheat on my whole field, about 10.5 mu — same as every year. I'll buy the improved wheat seeds from the village supply shop. I always buy improved, not the old varieties. The seeds are more reliable. I'll hire the rotary tiller before planting to break up the maize stubble — I can't do that by hand at my age. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and add urea at jointing. I irrigate four times: once at sowing to get the germination going, once before winter sets in, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide in early spring and do one fungicide spray before heading — powdery mildew has been bad some years.

**Maize (summer, starting June after wheat harvest):**
Right after wheat harvest, I direct-seed the maize — no tillage, no time. I buy hybrid maize seeds, everyone does now, the yields are much better. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress urea at the big bell stage. Summer has more rain so I only need to irrigate maybe three times — once at emergence if it's dry, once at silking, once at grain fill if August is hot and dry. I spray herbicide right after emergence and watch for corn borer — one pesticide application usually handles it.

I'm not trying anything new this year. The prices are uncertain and I can't afford a bad harvest.
